ledger.note: 888: territory. Infobox 'Gained territory: 888' (diocese 'Established: 3rd or 4th century'; the page: 'From 1111 the citizens of the city of Speyer began to increasingly loosen their bonds' and 'In 1294 Speyer became a Free Imperial City').
1644: Philippsburg. 'French troops captured Philippsburg in 1644' during the later stages of the Thirty Years' War.
1648: Philippsburg to France. 'France gained the fortress in the 1648 Peace of Westphalia.' Imperial troops recaptured it in 1676.
1648: the occupation of Philippsburg ends in cession: 'France gained the fortress in the 1648 Peace of Westphalia' (the loss event above).
1679: Philippsburg returned. At the Treaty of Nijmegen 'the fortress was officially returned to the Bishop and the Empire'.
1681: the left bank. 'France annexed parts of the bishopric's left-bank territories in 1681'; the page names no towns for the annexed parts, so the three left-bank circles stand in for them.
1688: Philippsburg seized again, 'at the beginning' of the Nine Years' War; 'the occupied territory was not returned until 1697'.
1697: the left bank returned. 'The occupied territory was not returned until 1697' (Treaty of Ryswick).
1697: Philippsburg returned with the other occupied territory.
1723: Bruchsal. The residence moved 'then in 1723 to Bruchsal' (infobox 'Bruchsal (from 1723)').

1801-1802: the left bank to France. 'The remaining left-bank territories of Speyer were conquered by French troops' (infobox 'Partitioned and secularised to France and Baden: 1801-03'; Mont-Tonnerre).
1803: secularised. 'It was secularized in 1803.' 'The right-bank territories went to margraves of Baden.'

certainty.note: The page gives an area (about 1,540 km2) and four towns; the circles are stand-ins and the 1681 annexation's extent is not on the page.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Speyer row.

SCOPE. 888 (infobox 'Gained territory') to 1803. The page's 'Established: 3rd or 4th century' is the diocese. Residences: Speyer to the 14th century, Udenheim from 1371 (text) or 1379 (infobox) to 1723, then Bruchsal. The page gives the French occupation of the 1790s only as the 1801/1802 conquest of the left bank; the 1815 division of the French part between Bavaria and Hesse-Darmstadt is after the state.

SHAPES. Bruchsal-Philippsburg 8.53E 49.18N 15 km; Deidesheim 8.19E 49.41N 9 km; Herxheim 8.20E 49.14N 10 km; Lauterburg 8.18E 48.98N 8 km; Philippsburg 8.46E 49.24N 6 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Bruchsal', 'Philippsburg', 'Deidesheim', 'Herxheim', 'Lauterburg'. The page does not name Kirrweiler.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Which left-bank parts were annexed in 1681; (2) the 1801 French conquest is entered at 1801 although the page gives '1801/1802'; (3) the 1371 / 1379 date for Udenheim.
